method.title: How it works
method.meta_description: The data, the 12 factors, the score formula, signal rules and how the track record is measured.
method.intro: FOMOMETER is a scoring tool for Solana memecoins. It does not use a neural network or a language model: the score is a transparent formula over public market data. This page describes exactly what it does and where it falls short.

data.title: Data
data.body: Every minute the engine reads DexScreener's boosted-token lists (top and latest boosts) and keeps the Solana tokens, up to 50. Boosts are paid promotion, so this is a list of promoted tokens, not of the most popular ones. For each token it records price, liquidity, fully diluted value, volume and buy/sell counts. Snapshots are kept for 72 hours.

factors.title: The 12 factors
factors.body: From the last 90 minutes of snapshots the engine computes 12 factors per token. Each factor is then standardized against all tokens in the same minute (a z-score capped at ±5), so a value says how unusual a token is compared with the rest of the list right now.

score.title: The score
score.body: The score is a weighted sum of 7 factors passed through a sigmoid, shown on the site as 0 to 100. The 7 factors are volume burst, buy pressure, reversal, liquidity depth, volume trend, RSI and deviation from average. The weights were fitted on past signals with a walk-forward random search. The other 5 factors are shown for context and do not change the score. The current weights are on the Strategy page.
score.regime: The engine also labels the market as neutral, bull, bear or panic from the spread of scores and volume trends across the list, and shifts the weights for volume burst, buy pressure and liquidity accordingly. The current regime is on the Strategy page.

signals.title: Signals
signals.body: Signals are events recorded when a token's score or volume crosses a threshold. They describe what happened in the data; they are not instructions to trade.

buy.name: BUY
buy.rule: The score rises from below the BUY threshold to at or above it.

sell.name: SELL
sell.rule: The score falls from at or above the BUY threshold to at or below the SELL threshold in one step. This is rare by design.

fomo.name: Volume burst
fomo.rule: The raw volume-burst factor exceeds its threshold: the 95th percentile of the last 6 hours, and never below 1.5. At most one per token every 30 minutes.

signals.thresholds: Thresholds are either fitted together with the weights or derived from recent score percentiles.
signals.thresholds_link: Current values are on the Strategy page.

gates.title: Quality filter
gates.body: A token can trigger signals only if it has at least 10 snapshots, at least $25,000 of liquidity, a buy/sell ratio between 0.8 and 3.0 over the last hour, and has not risen between 50% and 100% in the last hour. Tokens that fail are still scored and shown, they just cannot trigger signals.

record.title: Track record
record.body: 15 minutes, 1 hour and 4 hours after each signal the price change is recorded. The Strategy page shows how often the price moved in the signal's direction (up after BUY and volume burst, down after SELL) and the median change. Medians are used because a few extreme moves would dominate an average. Percentages are hidden when there are fewer than 20 outcomes.

limits.title: Limitations
limits.body: The track record has no fees and no slippage, and entry is the snapshot price. Since 15 October 2026 the engine keeps pricing a token for 4 hours after it leaves the list; before that, tokens that disappeared (often after a collapse) had no later price and dropped out, which flatters older results. The Strategy page shows how many outcomes still have no price, leaves out prices that jump more than 11 times (a switch to another pool), and compares every signal with all tracked tokens priced the same way. Samples are small and markets change, so past results say little about future ones. Scoring runs can fail or lag; the LIVE / STALE badge shows how fresh the data is. Nothing on this site is financial advice.

ret.label: 1-minute return

liq_score.label: Liquidity depth
liq_score.hint: Liquidity relative to fully diluted value, scaled to 0..1. Higher means a position is easier to exit.

pressure.label: Buy pressure
pressure.hint: Balance of buy and sell transactions over the last hour, from -1 (only sells) to +1 (only buys).

fomo.label: Volume burst
fomo.hint: Volume of the last 5 minutes compared with the pace of the last hour. Shows a sudden rush of trading.

dev.label: Deviation from average
dev.hint: How far the price is from its average over the last 20 snapshots.

vol_cluster.label: Volatility
vol_cluster.hint: Spread of 1-minute returns over the last 10 snapshots.

momentum_rev.label: Reversal
momentum_rev.hint: 1 when the last 5-minute move goes against the 5 minutes before it, otherwise 0.

rel_strength.label: RSI
rel_strength.hint: Relative strength index over 14 one-minute returns, rescaled to -1..1.

hl_range.label: 1-hour move
hl_range.hint: Size of the 1-hour price change reported by DexScreener, in either direction.

close_pos.label: Range position
close_pos.hint: Where the current price sits between the low and the high of the last 60 snapshots, 0..1.

vol_trend.label: Volume trend
vol_trend.hint: 1-hour volume compared with the hourly average over the last 6 hours.

summary.title: Summary
body: FOMOMETER scores Solana memecoins every minute from public market data and publishes how its past signals actually played out, including when they did badly. It is free and has no accounts.

Since 15 October 2026 it also earns: a Buy button opens a Jupiter swap in the visitor's own wallet, and each swap includes a 1% FOMOMETER fee. The $FMTR token will route that revenue back to holders: part paid out in SOL, part spent buying the token back and burning it. The track record stays as it is; revenue does not make the signals better than they are.

problem.title: The problem
body: Memecoin traders choose from thousands of new tokens a day. Raw data terminals show everything and rank nothing. Signal bots and callers rank everything and show no record: their calls are screenshots of winners, never a full list with the losers.
What is missing is a ranking whose method is public and whose every call is measured afterwards, so anyone can see how much to trust it.

product.title: What FOMOMETER does
steps: Reads DexScreener's boosted-token lists and keeps the Solana tokens, up to 50.
Computes 12 market factors per token from the last 90 minutes of data.
Compares each factor with the other tokens in the same minute, so a value means unusual compared with the rest of the list right now.
Combines 7 factors into a score from 0 to 100. Weights and thresholds are fitted on past outcomes and published on the Strategy page.
Records BUY, SELL and volume-burst events when thresholds are crossed, behind a quality filter.
Records the price 15 minutes, 1 hour and 4 hours after every event.
product.outro: No neural network or language model is involved.

evidence.title: Evidence so far
evidence.intro: Since 6 May 2026 the outcome of 45,618 events has been recorded (data as of 14 October 2026). Favorable means the price was higher afterwards, lower for SELL. Medians are used because a few broken prices produce averages of thousands of percent.
evidence.drawdown: Within 4 hours after a BUY, the worst point was a fall of 11% in the median case, and 16% of BUY tokens fell by half or more at some point.
evidence.baseline_intro: To see whether this beats picking at random, compare with every tracked token over the same 72 hours, one sample every 10 minutes:
evidence.reading: The promoted-token list loses value on average. BUY events pick tokens that are more often up an hour later than a random tracked token, but their median move is worse, and after 4 hours they do clearly worse than the baseline. The current score finds momentum that tends to reverse. It has no demonstrated trading edge, and the site does not claim one.
evidence.caveats: No fees or slippage. Tokens that leave the list have no later price and are left out, which flatters every row. Outcomes before 14 October 2026 could use a price taken after the horizon when a token had gaps. The method changed several times, so the all-time table mixes versions. These numbers are why signal research stays on the roadmap and why the site claims no edge.

items.name: Every call is recorded and scored
items.body: No deleting and no cherry-picking. The track record is computed from all events.

items.name: The method is public
items.body: Factors, formula, weights and thresholds are published. An edge, if one is found, has to come from doing the work well, not from secrecy.

items.name: No paid placement
items.body: Projects cannot pay to be scored higher, listed or featured. Revenue comes from users.

items.name: No custody
items.body: FOMOMETER never holds user funds or keys and does not trade for anyone. Swaps run in the user's own wallet.

items.name: No trading ahead of signals
items.body: The project never trades a token before its signal is public on the site.

items.name: Plain language
items.body: No claims of artificial intelligence, no guaranteed returns, no countdowns.

loop: People trade through the site; each swap pays a 1% fee into the pool.

Other project revenue, as it appears, joins the pool on its own line of the report.
50% of the pool buys $FMTR on the market every hour and burns it.

Fair launch on pump.fun. No presale, no private round.
One disclosed launch buy of at most 2%, locked for 6 months. No other team buys.
50% buyback and burn, 30% holder rewards in SOL, 20% operations and research.
Weekly, in SOL, pro rata to each wallet's average balance over the week. Minimum: tokens worth $20. Pools, the treasury, team and burn addresses are excluded.
Every hour, in small swaps through Jupiter at random minutes, from a 2-of-3 multisig treasury. Bought tokens are burned on chain.
Paying for Pro in $FMTR burns the whole payment.
Excluded from FOMOMETER's own board and signals.

rules: Rewards and buybacks are paid only from revenue already received, never from token sales, treasury tokens or borrowed money.
No revenue means no rewards and no buyback, and the report says so.
Every payment in, every reward and every burn is published with its transaction.
A change to these rules is announced 14 days ahead in a new version of this paper.
changes: Swap fees exist: version 0.1 had no revenue at all.
Holders now receive part of the revenue in SOL. Version 0.1 had buyback and burn only and said the token gives no claim on revenue.
Creator fees from trading $FMTR now go into the pool. Version 0.1 kept them out of buybacks.
Buybacks run every hour instead of weekly and take the largest share of the pool.
The token no longer waits for Pro and for the signal research to finish.

roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.body: Public launch and swaps are live; data integrity finishes in mid-November. Next come the $FMTR launch with a treasury page, signal research, then Pro and the API.

items.name: The signal may never work
items.body: Memecoins are close to a lottery with a negative drift. Research can end with no edge, and the site will say so. Swap revenue does not depend on the signals being good.

items.name: Revenue can be zero
items.body: Rewards and buybacks are a share of what the project earns. A quiet week means small or no payouts.

items.name: One data source
items.body: Everything comes from DexScreener. Outages or API changes stop the product.

items.name: Survivorship
items.body: Tokens that disappear are often the worst performers, and they are missing from the record.

items.name: Token risk
items.body: A token like this can lose most or all of its value whatever the product does. Rewards and buybacks do not set a floor.

items.name: Regulation
items.body: FOMOMETER is not based in the United States. Paying holders a share of revenue is regulated in many countries; rewards may exclude some of them, the United States included, and the rules of the project's own jurisdiction are checked before rewards start.
